headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: transformers can execute/write/network by default while awesome-prompts is an unverified prompt source that may be treated as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can be copied into transformers workflows. transformers can read files and run browsers/subprocesses, making prompt text a plausible instruction channel. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-prompts are pasted into a transformers-driven workflow without review, injection risk exists.
IF transformers parses repository content or generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled prompt text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Require manual review of any prompt text before use.
Strip executable-looking directives from copied prompts.
Use a separate read-only staging file for prompt content.
Add a human approval step before any tool action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No shared filesystem or secret-handling path is documented for awesome-prompts, and it has no data classes touched. transformers can read files and has broad network egress, but the pair lacks evidence of a shared sensitive workspace. The leakage pathway is therefore possible only through unusual operator setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files, transformers can read and potentially transmit them.
IF the operator copies sensitive content from another system into transformers inputs, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the two agents on separate workspaces.
Do not place secrets in directories readable by transformers.
Disable network access for transformers when handling sensitive files.
Use a throwaway test corpus for prompt experiments.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts itself is non-runnable, but transformers has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network capabilities. If both are used in the same directory or pipeline, transformers can overwrite or mutate artifacts that the prompt repository workflow depends on. Uncertainty about orchestration means we should choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF transformers and any wrapper around awesome-prompts share a writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF multiple transformers instances operate on the same files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Use separate output directories per run.
Run transformers with a read-only mount for prompt sources.
Serialize concurrent runs on shared artifacts.
Check in generated files only after diff review.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt source, so its content can become input to transformers. transformers can then generate downstream documents or actions from that input. Because no verification step is documented, the pair supports a classic unverified-input cascade, though not necessarily an automated action chain.
conditions: IF transformers consumes prompt text from awesome-prompts without a verification step, errors can propagate downstream.
IF generated text is reused as authoritative content, hallucinations or bad instructions can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of generated text.
Require citations or source links for factual claims.
Review outputs before any external publication.
Keep prompt-library content separate from final deliverables.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-prompts touches no data classes, and transformers' docs-only profile does not establish a compliance breach pathway by itself. With no evidence of regulated data flow, a compliance violation is not provable here.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into transformers and routed to a noncompliant deployment, compliance risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document data classification before use.
Review deployment residency and retention settings.
Use synthetic data for testing.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
